name: Training Datasets
blurb: Corpora used to pre-train models, with provenance and licence.

items.note: Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus; trained T5 and remains the most-downloaded classic pretraining set
15 trillion tokens of filtered CommonCrawl; the reference open web-scale pretraining corpus
The education-filtered FineWeb subset that lifted small-model benchmarks and set the quality-over-quantity pattern
The largest fully open corpus built from public-domain and permissioned text only
6TB of permissively-licensed source code behind StarCoder; gated with an opt-out process for authors
The 825GB corpus that defined open pretraining data in the GPT-Neo era; historically important, now superseded
AI2's 3-trillion-token corpus with full documentation of what went in and why; trained the OLMo models
Open reproduction of the LLaMA training mix

reading.body:
C4's download count exceeds the next seven datasets combined, making it the de facto baseline for researchers measuring data pipeline choices against a known reference point.

The eight datasets span roughly a decade of open pretraining practice, from The Pile's 825 gigabytes to FineWeb's 15 trillion tokens. That growth in scale is not merely archival ambition. Larger corpora demand proportionally more compute to process and train on, which means dataset choice is also an infrastructure choice: the corpus a team selects sets a floor on the GPU-hours, memory bandwidth, and storage capacity the training run requires before a single hyperparameter is tuned.

The more consequential pattern here may be qualitative rather than quantitative. FineWeb-Edu's download count sits close to FineWeb's despite being a filtered subset, and its note records that quality filtering lifted small-model benchmarks. Dolma's distinguishing feature is documentation of curation decisions rather than raw size. Both signal that practitioners are increasingly treating data quality as a lever that can substitute for compute, not just accompany it.

What this data does not cover is the training corpora behind the largest closed models, which are not publicly listed. The eight datasets here represent the open and documented fraction of the field. Licence terms vary, with two entries carrying no recorded licence at all, and The Stack's gating means its effective openness differs from the ungated majority. Download counts reflect researcher interest but not necessarily production use at training scale.
